alt: Online content flowing through AI into organized vector knowledge

text:
Impulse solves a simple problem: useful ideas are scattered across saved links. The application turns those sources into structured, searchable memory and grounded answers.

name: boundary-text
text: Target customers: students, creators, travelers and professionals who save useful content but cannot find or reuse it when needed.
textPreview: Target customers: students, creators, travelers and professionals who save useful content but cannot find or reuse it when needed.

text:
Saving a URL alone does not preserve meaning. The extension captures content, the Android application provides the user experience, and both rely on the same backend memory pipeline.

text: Stores structured memory plus a 768-value embedding.
textPreview: Stores structured memory plus a 768-value embedding.

name: backend-duty-body
text: PostgreSQL: URL, title, summary, category, tags, topics and actions   •   pgvector: 768 numbers representing semantic meaning
textPreview: PostgreSQL: URL, title, summary, category, tags, topics and actions   •   pgvector: 768 numbers representing semantic meaning

text:
The client never talks directly to the database or Gemini. Spring Boot validates the request, calls the FastAPI AI service, validates the returned 768-value embedding, and saves the memory.

text: The backend is the safety boundary
textPreview: The backend is the safety boundary

name: rag-formula-text
text: Before saving: required fields + exactly 768 embedding values. Before answering: correct user only, weak matches removed, duplicates removed, maximum 6 memories.
textPreview: Before saving: required fields + exactly 768 embedding values. Before answering: correct user only, weak matches removed, duplicates remo...

text:
The first LLM converts source content into reusable memory. At query time the question is embedded, hybrid retrieval ranks the user's memories, and only the best six are sent to the final LLM for a grounded response.

Future work adds audio and frame analysis, more approved sources, asynchronous processing, faster vector search, reranking, and stronger user controls. The core flow remains stable: understand, store, retrieve, then generate.
